request: How large is the immigration court backlog and how has it changed over time?

reply.reply:
**The immigration court backlog reached 3,558,995 pending cases at the end of FY2024; the evidence reviewed establishes its scale then but not a full year-by-year trend.**

- At FY2024 year-end, immigration courts had 3,558,995 pending cases; judges completed 701,749 cases that year while EOIR received an average of 148,663 new cases monthly. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- At FY2024 year-end, 1,478,623 asylum applications were pending in immigration courts. (IN12492, PDF p. 3)

Not yet covered: Historical annual total pending-case figures are needed to quantify the backlog's change over time; the report passage retrieved did not include those numbers.; A newer backlog total after FY2024 was not found in the reports opened.
reply.reasoning: CRS reports the FY2024 year-end total and that inflows substantially exceeded monthly completions that year. The latest staffing report gives judge staffing figures through FY2026 Q1, but not a later backlog count.
